name: Kind Hoopedge
description: Pinch the ring's inner rim between thumb and forefinger and let its weight hang to find the balance point.

name: Hoopblow
description: Throw the ring flat and level from the hip so it skims straight at the target's waist.

name: Diskdash
description: Cock the wrist back and snap it forward at release to give the ring its first hard spin.

name: Folded Spinrim
description: Slap a thrown ring aside with the flat of the palm before its edge can turn toward the hand.

name: Backward Bladering
description: Slide one foot back a half pace while the ring hand stays cocked and ready to throw.

name: Warm Disk
description: Run a thumb along the outer rim to feel for nicks that would pull the ring off its line.

name: Measured Outerblade
description: Rest the ring on the forefinger and spin it with small wrist flicks so it whirls without falling.

name: Calm Holeedge
description: Whirl the ring on the finger at an even slow rate while counting its turns to learn its rhythm.

name: Roundhit
description: Fling the whirling ring off the fingertip so it leaves already spinning and flies true.

name: Caromdodge
description: Drop to one knee and scoop a falling ring off the ground back onto the finger in one motion.

name: Mild Outerblade
description: Roll the wrist in slow circles with the ring held light so the joint loosens before throwing.

name: Kind Innergrip
description: Stand with feet shoulder-width and knees bent and the ring held at chest height to keep every throw level.

name: Gyratedash
description: Step forward and pitch the ring on a straight flat line to a marked post.

name: Sudden Carom
description: Lob the ring high over an obstacle so it drops edge first on the target behind it.

name: Bouncedrop
description: Throw the ring low so it skips off packed ground and rises into the target's shins.

name: Resting Innergrip
description: Raise a padded forearm to take a thrown ring on its flat so it rattles away unharmed.

name: Backward Ricochet
description: Duck and shift one pace sideways as a ring passes overhead while keeping your own ring ready.

name: Square Fingerhole
description: Alternate throws between two marker posts and reset the stance after each so the aim stays steady.

name: Mild Ringface
description: Mark the exact point in the arm's swing where the fingers open and release there every time.

name: Carombump
description: Toss a blunt practice quoit at a straw dummy to learn how a true hit sounds and feels.

name: Low Bladering
description: Grip the ring by its inner rim and slash across at arm's length with the outer edge.

name: Towing Bounce
description: Hook the ring's rim over an outstretched weapon hand and tug to pull it off line.

name: Diskskitter
description: Pivot a quarter turn on the ball of the foot to bring the throwing arm square to a new target.

name: Gentle Holeedge
description: Walk to the dummy after each round and read where the ring struck so the next throw is corrected.

name: Lowered Fingerhole
description: Pinch the returning ring's rim between two fingers as it slows and stop its spin without a cut.

name: Tight Roundedge
description: Let a rolled ring run up the forearm and stop against the crook of the elbow.

name: Ready Disk
description: Hook a spinning ring on one finger as it passes and ride its spin down to a stop.

name: Gyratehop
description: Step back as the ring drops short and reach out to meet it before it strikes the ground.

name: Open Ringface
description: Let a caught ring spin onto the wrist cuff and fling it back out in one continuous motion.

name: Smooth Spinrim
description: Close the eyes and listen for the ring's whir then reach out to catch it by sound alone.

name: Smooth Innergrip
description: Catch and release two practice rings in alternation to build a steady rhythm between the hands.

name: Calm Roundedge
description: Test the grip with a chilled hand to learn how the ring slips when the fingers are slow.

name: Ringface Count
description: Draw a thin thread of qi along the ring's outer rim so the edge bites cleaner on contact.

name: Grazeblow
description: Throw the ring with its rim turned toward the target so the edge and not the flat lands first.

name: Kind Outerblade
description: Feed qi into a ring spinning in the palm so it leaves the hand at full rate.

name: Kept Bladering
description: Catch an incoming blade on the ring's rim and turn it aside with a short wrist slap.

name: Swaying Ricochet
description: Glide a short pace forward on the ball of the foot while the ring arm swings through.

name: Deep Spinrim
description: Feel the ring's turning through the finger to judge how much of its force remains.

name: Diskdrop
description: Draw the ring from the opposite hip and throw across the body in a single sweep.

name: Rounddash
description: Lend qi to the ring at release so it holds its height and line over a longer flight.

name: Gyratedrop
description: Bring the ring down from above so its rim drops steeply onto a guarded target.

name: Bouncestrike
description: Hold the ring by its inner rim and cut backhand with the edge at close range.

name: Fingerhole Cowl
description: Turn the forearm so the ring's flat covers the wrist against a glancing cut.

name: Rounddodge
description: Pivot on the lead foot to leave the target's line of attack as the ring leaves the hand.

name: Steady Holeedge
description: Judge the distance by eye before the throw so the ring is neither short nor wasted.

name: Open Graze
description: Skim the ring flat just above the ground so it slides under a raised guard.

name: Hard Disk
description: Tilt the ring's plane at release so it begins low and curves upward into the target.

name: Settled Bladering
description: Tap a low incoming blade away with the ring's edge before it reaches the shin.

name: Bouncetrot
description: Skate backward on the rear foot to widen the gap just before a skimming throw.

name: Soft Roundedge
description: Watch dust and hanging cloth to read the air's push on the ring before releasing.

name: Deep Innergrip
description: Spin the ring around the wrist in slow circuits at first light to wake the joint.

name: Sharp Gyrate
description: Throw ten practice rings in a counted string with the stance reset after each release.

name: Firm Carom
description: Throw at a swinging target so the ring leads it by a body length and meets it.

name: Level Bounce
description: Draw the ring's edge down a hanging cord to learn how much pressure it takes to cut.

name: Bouncehop
description: Roll to the shoulder and rise with a dropped ring in hand and the stance already set.

name: Calm Disk
description: Pulse qi into the palm once per throw so the grip stays firm without strain.

name: Settled Hoopedge
description: Twist a cloth-wrapped forearm into a ring's path so the edge slides off harmlessly.

name: Watching Ringface
description: Cool down with a slow-spinning ring until the arm's tension fades and sore spots show.

name: Soft Fingerhole
description: Slide several rings onto the forearm in order so each one draws off cleanly from the stack.

name: Gnawing Graze
description: Draw the top ring from the stack and throw it in one smooth motion.

name: Roundblow
description: Throw a second ring close behind the first so the target must guard twice.

name: Grazetrot
description: Draw a ring from the belt as you step off the line so draw and dodge are one motion.

name: Judging Roundedge
description: Wrap the stacked rings in cord so they do not clink and warn a listening foe.

name: Resting Bladering
description: Hold a spare ring in the off hand to knock a thrown blade away.
